findings.quote: —though the Romans approved of their conduct—they finally surrendered
findings.problem: Greek: οὐδενὸς βοηθοῦντος, συνευδοκούντων Ῥωμαίων παρέδοσαν ἑαυτούς — the Romans consenting (genitive absolute), they surrendered. The Romans' consent was to the surrender; the English makes it a concessive 'though' about their conduct.
findings.proposed_fix: , they finally surrendered with the Romans’ consent

findings.quote: But Hieronymus, already leaning strongly toward the Carthaginians, said
findings.problem: Greek: ὁ δ᾽ Ἱερώνυμος ἔτ᾽ ἐγγὺς ἐπόντων τῶν πρεσβευτῶν [εἴτ᾽ ἐν μισειόντων] τῶν Καρχηδονίων — the text is corrupt (editor's bracket) but the sense is that the Carthaginian envoys were still at hand/present; nothing says he was 'leaning' toward them. The English smooths a corrupt passage into an invented statement.
findings.proposed_fix: But Hieronymus, while the Carthaginian envoys were still at hand (the Greek here is corrupt), said

units.note: Greek corrupt at this point; fix preserves the uncertainty.

findings.quote: whom all the Siceliots alone had willingly and deliberately approved as their leader and king
findings.problem: Greek: ὃν μόνον κατὰ προαίρεσιν καὶ κατ᾽ εὔνοιαν Σικελιῶται πάντες εὐδόκησαν σφῶν αὐτῶν ἡγεμόν᾽ εἶναι καὶ βασιλέα — μόνον agrees with ὃν (Pyrrhus): he was the only man whom all the Siceliots willingly approved. The English attaches 'alone' to the Siceliots.
findings.proposed_fix: the only man whom all the Siceliots had willingly and deliberately approved as their leader and king

units.note: Greek breaks off mid-sentence (τοῖς φιλομαθοῦσι); English marks the gap with [...].
